must.rule: `<cli> help --json` prints one JSON document that names every command.
must.why: An agent learns the interface from the interface. Help that parses lets it list commands without scraping prose.

must.rule: Help says who sees each command: only the person, or other people.
must.why: The one thing an agent must know before acting is whether other people will see it.

must.rule: Every command the CLI registers is listed once in `help --json` and in the inventory the adopter generates from its command registration, and the X-ray covers exactly that set.
must.why: A conformance report is only as good as its coverage: a command nobody listed is never checked.

must.rule: Exit codes are documented, and every exit code the CLI gives is one of them.
must.why: Stable, documented exit codes let an agent branch without parsing prose.

must.rule: An unknown flag fails before anything runs, and the error names the flag.
must.why: A silently ignored flag gives an agent a wrong answer that looks right: `--limt 2` returns everything.
must.found: `app today --ax-xray-no-such-flag --json` → exit 0; stdout: {: the flag was ignored

must.rule: Ambiguous verbs (edit, delete, remove) don't act; they answer with the specific commands.
must.why: `edit` could mean a private draft or a message others already saw; guessing is how agents do the wrong thing.

must.rule: Every command other people see refuses to run without `--why`, and says so.
must.why: What others see is logged with who asked and why.

must.rule: A wrong reference fails before anything reaches anyone, and the error says where to get a right one.
must.why: Checking before acting keeps a stale id from becoming a wrong message.

must.rule: Every command other people see has a preview that acts on nothing (`--dry-run`) and names who will see it.
must.why: An agent, or a checker, can confirm the audience without acting; a wall it is not, because nothing waits on it.
must.found: `app send --help` offers no --dry-run, so who will see it can only be learnt by doing it

must.rule: A command that takes free text accepts it as one argument, not only on stdin, and its help shows that form.
must.why: An agent allowed to run only this CLI (`shell(<cli>)`) cannot pipe into it: the pipe's first command is not the CLI, so the call is denied.

must.rule: A wait command accepts the refs the reads list: `watch <ref>` waits on the conversation a list gave.
must.why: Waiting through the interface beats polling; when the wait refuses the ref the agent holds, agents fall back to blind streams and pollers.
must.found: `app watch c:00000000bbbb0000bbbb000000000002 --timeout 1s` → exit 2; stderr: app: watch takes an object ref such as meeting:<ref>; bare "watch" streams every event

must.why: An agent must be able to look freely.

must.rule: A refused call changes nothing, except an audit record that says it was refused.
must.why: An agent that gets the call wrong must be able to try again safely.

must.rule: Every route the agent port registers is in the inventory the adopter generates from its router, once, and the X-ray's routes manifest covers exactly that set.
must.why: A route nobody listed is never checked.

must.rule: A route given an id that does not exist fails and says where to get a right one.
must.why: Checking before acting keeps a stale id from becoming a wrong write.

must.rule: Every route that does what other people see refuses a request without a why, and names the field.
must.why: What others see is logged with who asked and why.
An agent must be able to look freely.

must.rule: A refused request changes nothing, except an audit record that says it was refused.
must.why: An agent that gets the request wrong must be able to try again safely.
